summary.text: Khanh Pham is a Democratic member of the Oregon State Senate for District 23, which her biography describes as the Jade District and southeast and northeast Portland.
She was first elected to the Oregon House in 2020 and chairs the Senate Housing and Development Committee.

paragraphs.text: Pham was the first Vietnamese American legislator in the Oregon legislature, according to her biography.
She also serves on the Senate Energy and Environment Committee, the Senate Labor and Business Committee and the Joint Committees on Transportation.

Before entering the legislature she was a founding leader of and spokesperson for the Portland Clean Energy Fund initiative, which passed in November 2018, and served as interim alliance director at the Oregon Just Transition Alliance.
She previously was environmental justice manager at the Asian Pacific American Network of Oregon.
She holds a bachelor's degree from Lewis & Clark College and a master's degree in urban studies from Portland State University.
Her page says she championed the 2021 Oregon Clean Energy Opportunity bills and co-led the effort to refer statewide ranked choice voting to the 2024 Oregon ballot.
